title: Etale purity across a regular integral Cartier divisor
statement: Let $L$ be locally Noetherian and $i:D\to L$ an effective Cartier centre [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] with $D$ regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] and integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $U\subseteq L$ be the open complement of the image of $i$. Let $n:N\to L$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] over $U$. Suppose $W\subseteq L$ is open, contains the image of the generic point of $D$, and $n$ is etale over $W$. Then there are a finite etale $p:E\to L$ and an isomorphism $N|_U\cong E|_U$ over $U$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or normality of $N$ is assumed.

proof.text: Set V=U union W. The boundary calculation gives regular local stalks of dimension at least two outside V.

Etaleness is local at the target. Cover V by its inverse images of U and W; the twice-restricted arrows are isomorphic to n restricted to U and W. The supplied etaleness therefore gives Etale(n restricted to V). Finiteness is preserved by this base change.

Apply finite-etale extension across a regular codimension-two boundary to q=n restricted to V. Obtain finite etale p:E to L and an isomorphism over V. Restrict that isomorphism to U using preimageIso and the isoOfLE identifications of nested opens. The equation over V identifies the preimages of U; cancelling the inclusion U into L proves the required equation over U.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0EYE and 0EYJ, factoring the extension through U union W and the codimension-two final step of 0H2W.
